one_liner: Cloud communications APIs for SMS, voice, video, and email

evidence.claim: Twilio APIs authenticate via HTTP Basic auth using an API Key/Secret (recommended) or Account SID/Auth Token
evidence.quote: To authenticate requests to the Twilio APIs, Twilio supports [HTTP Basic authentication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication).

evidence.claim: Developers can self-serve create API keys via the Console or REST API
evidence.quote: You can create an API key either [in the Twilio Console](/docs/iam/api-keys/keys-in-console) or [using the API](/docs/iam/api-keys/key-resource-v1).

evidence.claim: Twilio also supports OAuth 2.0 (Client Credentials and Authorization Code grants) with bearer access tokens
evidence.quote: Twilio supports two OAuth 2.0 grant types: **Client Credentials** and **Authorization Code**.

evidence.claim: OAuth apps are available to all accounts at no extra cost, indicating no paid gate for credentials
evidence.quote: OAuth apps are available to all accounts at no additional cost.

evidence.claim: The API surface is very large and Twilio hosts an official MCP server
evidence.quote: direct, structured access to Twilio's full API surface—over 1,800 endpoints across 30+ products

notes: Official MCP server exists at mcp.twilio.com/docs but it is read-only docs/spec search (twilio__search, twilio__retrieve) and does not execute API calls; it requires no auth. GraphQL surface exists only via Twilio Flex per third-party spec; platform is REST-first. Credentials are region-specific (region + edge flags). Material doesn't explicitly state trial terms, but console self-serve credential creation and no-cost OAuth apps confirm no approval/sales gate; Twilio's standard signup is a trial account with credentials.
